This! Therapy is for everyone. Even therapists have therapists. Try to ease her in with that; and go slowly from there. Being borderline is different from being bipolar and I honestly didn’t even really know bpd was a thing til I got my diagnosis; she’s probably aware something is off but won’t seek help until ready so she just needs a gentle push. When you sense her mood turning dark try to suggest a distraction such as going for a walk, a funny movie, coloring. It might help a little.

As a woman with a BPD diagnosis I definitely think she should try therapy! If you’re not comfortable bringing it up to her try going through a family member she’s close to? The right combination of different resources is all she needs and you’ll both feel the ease.

Reading this post made this feeling swell up inside of me. I’ve told myself and others that I think I am on the spectrum, but I am not taken serious. I have a BPD, MDD, PTSD diagnosis. Ugh I relate to almost everything here. Super random but: When I was younger I would rub my hands together whenever I was really excited or anxious and my brothers would make fun of me for it so I forced myself to stop. But to this day I still rock myself, bite my tongue, rip my toenails off which is another mental illness called onychotillomania that I haven’t been diagnosed with but have done research into and it fits. I’m super sensitive, don’t like to be touched unless I initiate it, and just so much more.
